description.narrative: The overall objective of the Development intervention is: (1) to ensure that the largest number of un- and under-banked low-income women are served well with both existing and new financial products and services; and (2) Strengthen financial institutions through leadership development and build gender diversity within them.
The contribution supports WWB´s Strategic Plan for the period 2014-17.

Women´s World Banking är en internationell organisation som sedan 35 år främjar kvinnors tillgång till finansiella tjänster, såsom sparande, krediter, försäkring m m, via ett nätverk med 39 finansiella institutioner (företrädesvis mikrofinans) i 28 länder. Sida har stött organisationen sedan 2008 och det nu planerade stödet avser den strategiska planen för perioden 2014-2016 vilket dock förlängts i ett ytterligare år till år 2017. Detta motiveras av att allt tillgängligt kärnstöd annars upphör vid samma tidpunkt och är möjligt att godkänna eftersom resultatramverket har anpassats till att inkludera detta år.
Den nu aktuella strategiska planen innebär ett fortsatt fokus på att nå högsta möjliga antal kvinnor med låg inkomst, som idag inte omfattas, med anpassade produkter och tjänster samt att stärka finansiella institutioner genom ledarskapsutveckling med ett jämställdhetsfokus.

The Agreement period that now comes to an end covers the previous strategy (2014-2016) including the first year of the new strategy (2017). An evaluation was carried out in the end of the agreement period that would feed into the new strategy (2017-2021). The main reason for the inclusion of one additional year in Sida´s support was to bridge the overall financial transition into the new strategy. An additional benefit is that the findings from the evaluation can be "harvested" into this conclusion. The overall conclusion was that WWB achieved several key successes, but also faced certain challenges. Key organizational achievements: * Developed new products and reached about 650 000 women clients across savings, credit and insurance. * Improved fundraising to achieve more stable financial standing. * Strengthened organizational M&E through refinement of institutional dashboard that is more comprehensive. * Continued to develop global footprint through diversification and extension of network and investments. * Developed Leadership and Diversity for Innovation Program to show clearer link between a program and business outcomes. These results were generally speaking expected. Based on the assessment the evaluator identified a number of potential implications that informed the design of the future strategy.
